archetype.name: Pocket Passer (sack-averse rhythm thrower)
archetype.definition: A veteran timing passer who wins underneath and on schedule, rarely takes a sack, and is fed volume by two strong outside receivers, but whose intermediate throws have always carried interception risk.

report.headline: Volume is real, efficiency is sliding; Philadelphia's thin pass rush offers a reset.
report.take:
Prescott in 2026 is a high-volume version of the quarterback he has been for a decade: on schedule, ball out at 2.74 seconds, short and quick game first, with Lamb and Pickens doing most of the damage. His 273.2 yards a game ranks 6th, but 6.66 yards per attempt ranks 25th, down 0.93 from last year's 7.59. Those yards come from attempts, not from explosiveness. Dallas throws 41 times a game because its defense is 31st in EPA and dead last against the pass. Most weeks, the offense has to keep scoring to stay in the game.

The engine is the short game. On throws of 0-9 air yards he is at +0.284 EPA with a 74.6% completion rate and +4.5 CPOE, which is efficient and repeatable. The pocket work is the best in the league by one measure: a 2.8% sack rate ranks 1st, and only 11.5% of his pressures become sacks. That is not a scrambler extending plays. He gets rid of it, and the cost shows up as throwaways and checkdowns rather than drive-killing losses. The leak is the 10-19 yard window: a 50% completion rate, -4.2 CPOE, and four of his five interceptions. Add three interceptions over the middle on just 45 attempts, and you have a quarterback whose mistakes cluster on throws into traffic.

The headline efficiency also flatters him a little. His +0.22 EPA when trailing by 9 or more is far better than the +0.055 he posts in one-score states, so some of the production comes against softer, protect-the-lead coverage. Ferguson has been a drain at -0.251 EPA per target. The last three games are the real worry. EPA per dropback fell to -0.013, CPOE to -3.3, and he threw four interceptions while averaging 47 attempts.

Context softens that slide but doesn't erase it. Two of those games came against Tampa Bay (4th-ranked defense, on a four-day turnaround) and Green Bay (11th). His career also shows his interception totals ranking poorly most years, so the turnovers are part of who he is rather than a new collapse. The core skills of accuracy underneath and sack avoidance have held across seasons. Expect the efficiency to settle back toward the middle of the league rather than stay at the bottom.

strengths.title: Best sack avoidance in football
strengths.body: His 2.8% sack rate ranks 1st of 45, and his pressure-to-sack rate ranks 2nd. It comes from a quick, decisive release, not from a great line alone. That trait has made him one of the better pressure-to-sack quarterbacks in most seasons, so it should hold.

strengths.title: Efficient short-area accuracy
strengths.body: Throws under 10 air yards are his bread and butter: +0.284 EPA, a 54.5% success rate and +4.5 CPOE on 134 attempts. This is a big sample and a long-held skill, and it keeps the offense on schedule even when the downfield game sputters.

strengths.title: Two outside receivers carrying the load
strengths.body: Lamb (+0.345 per target) and Pickens (+0.395) are both producing at a high rate on heavy volume. Having two separators outside lets Prescott play rhythm football and still find chunk plays. As long as both stay healthy, this supports his floor.

concerns.title: Three-game efficiency slide
concerns.body: Over Weeks 4-6 his EPA per dropback fell to -0.013 and his CPOE to -3.3, with four interceptions while throwing 47 times a game. Some of it is the opposition: Tampa Bay's defense ranks 4th, and that game came on short rest. Still, the drop is steep enough to watch rather than dismiss.

concerns.title: Intermediate and middle-field turnovers
concerns.body: Four of his five interceptions came on 10-19 yard throws, where he completes only 50%. Three came over the middle on 45 attempts. His career interception ranks have been poor in most seasons, so this is a long-standing cost of how he attacks windows rather than a fluke, and it will keep showing up.

concerns.title: Yards inflated by game script
concerns.body: Per-attempt efficiency is below average and down from last year. The yardage total leans on Dallas trailing and throwing, since his EPA when down two scores far exceeds his one-score production. If the defense ever stabilizes, the volume could shrink faster than the efficiency improves.

trend.note: He opened with three strong EPA games, then faded: a modest Week 4 in Houston, followed by negative-EPA outings against Tampa Bay and Green Bay, even as attempts climbed past 40 a game.

nextGame.headline: Weak Eagles rush and a Hurts-less offense tilt this Dallas's way
nextGame.body:
Philadelphia's defense ranks 24th against the pass and generates almost no heat: 32nd in hit rate and 31st in sack rate. That suits a quick-release passer who already rarely goes down. The soft spot is WR1, where the Eagles allow +0.54 EPA a play (28th), which points straight at Lamb. Where they hold up is deep (9th in deep EPA), so expect Prescott's usual short-and-intermediate diet rather than a shot-heavy plan. The Book makes Dallas a 4.5-point road favorite with a 44.5 total, lower than any total Dallas has seen this year. That suggests fewer forced-comeback attempts than usual.

Availability matters mostly on the other side. Jalen Hurts is out for the season, Saquon Barkley is out, and the line is missing Lane Johnson and Landon Dickerson, which keeps an offense already 28th in EPA stuck in neutral. On defense, edge rusher Jalyx Hunt is out, Nolan Smith Jr. is questionable after a concussion, and AJ Epenesa is out, thinning an already weak rush. Slot corner Michael Carter II is also out. For Dallas, only KaVontae Turpin (ribs, a 15%-snap gadget role) is expected to miss, which barely touches the passing game.

keyMatchups.title: Lamb against a leaky WR1 defense
keyMatchups.body: Philadelphia has let opposing WR1s beat their averages by 3 PPR points a game, at +0.54 EPA per play. Lamb's 71 targets and +0.345 per target make him the obvious funnel, and Prescott leans to the left side, where his EPA is strongest.

keyMatchups.title: Depleted Eagles pass rush
keyMatchups.body: The Eagles already rank last in hit rate, and their edge group is short-handed. That should give Prescott clean pockets and favors his short-game rhythm, the area where he is most efficient.

keyMatchups.title: Game script without Hurts
keyMatchups.body: With Philadelphia's offense this compromised, Dallas may play with a lead. That could trim the 47-attempt volume of recent weeks while lifting efficiency. A lower ceiling on yards but a better chance at clean, mistake-free football.

nextGame.watch: Whether his 10-19 yard throws stop finding defenders. A clean intermediate game against a weak rush would mark the slide as opponent-driven.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume should hold as long as Dallas's pass defense stays at the bottom of the league. His sack avoidance and short-game accuracy are long-standing traits, so his floor is steady. Efficiency should rebound from the last-three-game trough toward the season's middle-of-the-pack level. Expect it to land there, not at last year's top-15 per-attempt rate, given the yards-per-attempt decline. Interceptions will keep coming at roughly his career norm because of where he throws them.

Realistically, that means about 255-295 passing yards a game, around 1.4-2.0 touchdowns, and 0.6-0.9 interceptions. Red-zone touchdown production is the most fragile piece: nine scores on a low success rate leans on finishing plays that may not repeat at that clip.
swingFactors: Whether Dallas's last-ranked pass defense forces more shootouts

confidence.note: Six games; the recent slide overlaps tougher defenses and short rest.
